All industries ↗

Keep the commercial promise attached

Professional services teams move from opportunity to proposal, signed scope, staffing, delivery, and billing. Important details can disappear at each handoff. Maia can prepare a source-linked brief in Slack that keeps the client's goal, agreed deliverables, dependencies, and open questions together.

The responsible professional still interprets scope, commits resources, advises the client, and approves communication. Maia makes the source material easier to review.

Prepare a proposal outline

Provide the opportunity record, discovery notes, approved service descriptions, prior examples, and the proposal template. Maia can organize known facts, identify missing inputs, and draft an outline without inventing credentials or commitments.

The partner chooses scope, approach, fees, team, timeline, and claims. Missing client context becomes a question for discovery rather than a polished assumption in the proposal.

Turn a signed scope into a kickoff brief

Give Maia the signed statement of work, project notes, and relevant operating guidance. It can extract deliverables, dates, dependencies, client responsibilities, and ambiguous language with page citations.

The project lead verifies the interpretation and assigns work. Contract meaning and legal questions stay with qualified reviewers. A clear kickoff brief helps the delivery team see what was actually agreed.

Improve the sales-to-delivery handoff

Combine the CRM record, proposal, signed scope, meeting notes, stakeholder list, and delivery template. Maia can structure the client's goal, commitments, owners, risks, and unresolved questions in one thread.

Account and delivery owners accept the handoff together. If a promise appears in sales notes but not in the signed record, the discrepancy remains visible until they resolve it.

Review engagement health

Provide project milestones, recent decisions, client dependencies, scope questions, and selected financial inputs. Maia can prepare a weekly review covering progress, overdue decisions, upcoming client moments, and potential scope pressure.

The engagement lead decides whether to change staffing, escalate a risk, or speak with the client. Maia should quote the relevant record, not declare a request out of scope.

Start with one engagement

Choose one proposal, signed scope, and project plan with an ambiguous dependency. Ask Maia for the cited kickoff brief, then have the project lead resolve the dependency before assigning the delivery work.

Once kickoff decisions are confirmed, Maia can draft the corresponding project records and client recap for review. The delivery team sees the agreed owners and milestones, while the relationship lead checks that the message reflects the signed scope and current client conversation.

At the next engagement review, Maia can focus on changed milestones, overdue client inputs, and new scope questions. That makes the brief useful throughout delivery rather than only at handoff.

Questions from services firms

Can Maia read contracts and statements of work?

It can work with authorized files and cite the relevant pages. The engagement owner verifies dates, deliverables, and interpretation.

Can each engagement stay separate?

Use separate channels, approved source sets, and appropriate access for each client. Do not reuse one engagement's private context in another.

Does Maia provide professional or legal advice?

No. Maia prepares records and drafts. Qualified professionals retain analysis, advice, and client accountability.
